VERSE_1 = "fly"

# Each verse is keyed by the animal swallowed in that verse, in order.
# The value is the second line of the verse (the animal-specific comment).
# The fly verse has no comment line.
ANIMALS = ["fly", "spider", "bird", "cat", "dog", "goat", "cow", "horse"]

COMMENTS = {
    "spider": "It wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her.",
    "bird": "How absurd to swallow a bird!",
    "cat": "Imagine that, to swallow a cat!",
    "dog": "What a hog, to swallow a dog!",
    "goat": "Just opened her throat and swallowed a goat!",
    "cow": "I don't know how she swallowed a cow!",
    "horse": "She's dead, of course!",
}

# When the bird is swallowed, the spider is described with this phrase.
SPIDER_REF = "the spider that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her"


def _verse(verse_number):
    animal = ANIMALS[verse_number - 1]
    lines = [f"I know an old lady who swallowed a {animal}."]

    comment = COMMENTS.get(animal)
    if comment is not None:
        lines.append(comment)

    # The horse is the last verse: no chain follows.
    if animal == "horse":
        return lines

    # Walk the chain backwards from this animal down to the fly.
    for caught in reversed(ANIMALS[: verse_number - 1]):
        if caught == "spider":
            lines.append(f"She swallowed the {animal} to catch {SPIDER_REF}.")
            animal = "spider"
        else:
            lines.append(f"She swallowed the {animal} to catch the {caught}.")
            animal = caught

    lines.append("I don't know why she swallowed the fly. Perhaps she'll die.")
    return lines


def recite(start_verse, end_verse):
    verses = [_verse(n) for n in range(start_verse, end_verse + 1)]
    lines = []
    for i, verse in enumerate(verses):
        if i > 0:
            lines.append("")
        lines.extend(verse)
    return lines
